data.short_meaning: To value, to prize, to hold dear
data.long_meaning: The name Cherish is derived from the Old English word 'ceorisan', meaning 'to value, to prize, to hold dear'. This name was commonly given to children born to parents who deeply cherished and loved their offspring. The name Cherish carries the meaning “To value, to prize, to hold dear” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Cherish usually hope their child will grow to embody to value, to prize, to hold dear and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: To cherish and protect the gift of life.
data.etymology: Cherish belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “To value, to prize, to hold dear.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cherish total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: חבר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: חבר: עברית שם שמחה, קשור לאהבה, חיבה, ואהדה. השם קשור לבראשית 3:6, 'וה'אדוני יאהב אותך'. חבר הוא שם נפוץ בישראל, משפחות, ובעלי חיים.

in_greek.name: Ἀγάπη
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἀγάπη: Ἑλληνικό πρέπον, συνδεόμενο με ἀγάπη, φιλία, καὶ εὐλάβεια. Ἡ λέξη συνδέεται με τὸν Ἰησοῦν, ὅς εἶπε, «Ἀγάπη τοῦτο ἐστὶν ἵνα ποιήσωμεν τὰ ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ» (Γαλάτεια 14:21). Ἀγάπη ἔχει πλούσια ἱστορία στὴν Ἑλληνικὴ καὶ τὴν Χριστιανικὴ παράδοση.

in_latin.name: Caritas
in_latin.long_meaning: Caritas: Latinum nomen, caritatis significans, amoris, et pietatis. Nomen hic caritas originem trahit ex caritas, quae est amor, benignitas, et humanitas. In Ecclesia Latina, caritas significat amorem divinum et humanum. Caritas est nomen antiquum, quod in Novo Testamento invenitur, ubi dictum est, "Caritas Dei habitat in nobis" (1 Ioannis 4:12).

in_english.long_meaning: Cherish: English name, derived from the Old French word 'cherir', meaning to love, hold dear, and respect. The name Cherish has a rich history in Christian tradition, symbolizing the love and care of God for humanity. In the Bible, the concept of cherishing is seen in Jesus' teaching, "Love your neighbor as yourself" (Mark 12:31). Cherish is a popular name in modern Christian cultures, often associated with qualities like kindness, compassion, and devotion.
